title: unify-remote-build-cache-and-upgrade-buildkit-tooling
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
Unify disparate build caches across Docker/npm/Go/Rust pipelines behind a resilient remote cache proxy, upgrade BuildKit to latest stable for improved layer reuse and parallelism, and standardize developer toolchain wrappers (sccache for Rust, npm ci flags, hermetic yarn cache). Goal is lower median developer build time by >=30% and reduce CI egress/storage costs by >=25%.

Background:
We currently have multiple cache strategies (per-repo Docker registries, ephemeral GitHub Actions caches, ad-hoc s3 caches for different languages). This causes inconsistent cache hit rates, slower developer iteration, and unpredictable CI costs. BuildKit v0.10 is used in many pipelines but misses performance fixes and security patches shipped in v0.11+. Rust builds are not using sccache consistently which causes repeated compilation for CI matrix jobs. Node installs are not pinned or using centralized cache, causing long install times.

Scope of work:
- Deploy a remote build cache proxy (s3-backed, signed uploads, TTL-based eviction) fronted by a small fleet of cache proxy workers in our infra.
- Migrate Docker/BuildKit pipelines to push/pull layer caches to the new proxy via BuildKit's inline cache and registry fallback support.
- Upgrade BuildKit on all CI runners to v0.11.x and validate kernel/OCI compat on dedicated runners.
- Introduce sccache as an opt-out wrapper for Rust targets and document integration for local dev.
- Add hermetic npm/yarn caching using a shared pnpm-cache artifact for the most active monorepos; standardize npm ci + package-lock consistency checks.
- Create a rollout plan per repo group (core infra, runtime, SDKs, web) with canaries and observability.

Success metrics and monitoring:
- Median cold build time for core services down 30% within 6 weeks of rollout (tracked via build-duration dashboard).
- CI tokenized egress/storage cost down 25% month-over-month after stabilization.
- Cache hit ratio >= 70% for Docker layer cache on repeated PRs for targeted repos.
- No increase in flaky CI failures due to cache corruption; monitor via flaky-job-rate.

Milestones:
1) Prototype remote cache proxy and BuildKit v0.11 integration (Proof of concept) — COMPLETE 2026-02-05
   - Benchmarks: 45% faster layer reuse on simple rails service; sccache reduced incremental Rust build time by 60% locally.
   - PoC artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/remote-build-cache-poc and PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1223
2) Implement cache proxy with signed uploads + TTL and promote to staging runners — COMPLETE 2026-02-24
   - Logging and metrics: buildcache.put/get latency, key eviction counts, validation errors.
3) Rollout BuildKit upgrade to dedicated runners + compatibility smoke tests — IN PROGRESS 2026-03-10
   - Compatibility checklist: overlayfs tests, manifest v2 handling, unsupported flags audit.
4) Repo-by-repo migration, starting with infra/serving/runtime and SDKs — PLANNED Q2 2026

Decisions and trade-offs:
- Use S3-backed object store with signed manifests for persistence (trade-off: latency vs durability). We accept slightly higher put latency to ensure consistent cache persistence across runner autoscaling events.
- Prefer BuildKit v0.11.x rather than patching existing v0.10 due to improved cache key stability and parallel session handling. Some older runners will remain on v0.10 during a staggered upgrade window.
- sccache is adopted as opt-out to reduce friction for teams; we will enable it for CI by default and document when to disable (e.g., problematic cross-compiled targets).

Rollout & Risk Mitigation:
- Canary plan: migrate 2 low-traffic repos first, measure cache hit rates and flakiness for 2 weeks, then expand to core infra repos.
- Automated rollback: if cache-related failures exceed threshold (5% more flaky jobs for two consecutive days), revert BuildKit runner pool to previous image and route traffic back to ephemeral caches.
- Validation: integrate small verification step in CI that pulls a known cache key and validates manifest signatures to detect corruption early.

Open blockers:
- Docker registry permission model for inline-cache pushes requires a service account update (INF-OPS ticket: https://internal.redwood.ai/t/INFOPS-924).
- Need legal sign-off for cross-region cache replication (privacy/compliance question).

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Unified+Build+Cache+Design
- PoC infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1223
- BuildKit upgrade automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-scripts/pull/88
- Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ci-builds/ci-build-duration

Follow-ups and next steps:
- Add per-repo cache tagging to support multi-tenant eviction policies.
- Explore immutable base images signed with cosign to reduce layer trust issues.
- Investigate migrating heavy test matrices to persistent runners to better benefit from cache persistence.
